newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed, spreads to U.S. narrow.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed, spreads to U.S. narrow.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed in thin trade on Tuesday, with spreads to U.S. bonds falling sharply even as the Canadian market took its direction from U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.

"The price action today was mainly following the U.S. The Fed speech was a little bit hawkish," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "It was a good day for Canada relative to the U.S. bonds."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 fell C$0.10 to C$101.40 to yield 7.872 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 16/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 76 basis points from 81 basis points at Monday's close.
Spreads narrowed sharply after breaking through a key technical resistance level, Kalirai said.
"We took those out today so technically and fundamentally I think the Canadian market looks very good right now for further spread narrowing," said Kalirai.

Both Canadian and U.S. long bonds lost gains made early in the session and closed weaker. The weakness followed comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Janet Yellen. She said the U.S. economy has entered "an inflationary danger zone."

Investors are now looking ahead to release of key economic data later this week, including U.S. Federal Reserve Beige Book on Wednesday and Canadian and U.S. consumer price data on Friday, analysts said.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.06 to C$97.09 to yield 7.409 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 10/32 to yield 6.92 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 49 basis points from 53 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.87 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.29 percent.
